content:
In early July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be well received, but the same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't too affected by this bug. Because of that, I initially thought this TestFlight update was a simple but meaningful improvement.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta apps, and the latest TestFlight update is a perfect example. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds a "search bar, making it easy to quickly search for apps."

Looking back, I did notice some strange occurrences, which I also mentioned at the bottom of the article (though my understanding at the time was completely the opposite):

I think the reason I didn't realise this was a bug is because I kept all the TestFlight beta apps I've installed over the years, with the goal of "merging" my previously separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It's not the most convenient approach, but for me it's been worth it.

In any case, this TestFlight bug didn't escape the notice of John Vorhees at MacStories:

So, you can imagine how thrilled I was when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac about TestFlight adding a search bar. I thought: "Finally!" I immediately put aside what I was doing to update the app. [...] Unfortunately, there's a big "but" here. Previously, beta versions in TestFlight were arranged in reverse chronological order, which I personally really liked. [...] Now, expired beta versions and still-active TestFlight betas are mixed together alphabetically in the list, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I roughly counted around 800 app entries for me. As you can imagine, only a very small number of those are actually active betas. The search function does help, but it's no longer possible to scroll through to find things.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and this bug on Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update did indeed fix the relevant bug.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix for users affected by this regression issue.
